_about: Spoken narration for the /fitness chapter "skills" (owner, 2026-10-01: "our fitness one needs this too", after hearing the MetFix Module 1 and 2 narration; amendment H.75). Its own script, not the captions: one paragraph per beat explaining what is on screen, in the order the picture builds, every sentence restating the lesson's own text (fitnessData.ts: INTRO_TEXT, DEFINITION_TEXT, POWER_CONCEPT, MODULE_COPY, SKILLS, ARCHETYPES, HOPPER_DOMAINS, ENERGY_SYSTEMS, ENERGY_BENCHMARKS, CONTINUUM_EXAMPLES) and the captions, no new facts or numbers; each beat names its passage. The voice is Charon. Edit a sentence and narration-check fails until its clip is regenerated (voice/ pipeline), copied into public/narration/fitness/skills/ and node scripts/narration-manifest.mjs has run. Plain hyphens only.

gates.why: Paragraph narration breathes between sentences (the owner-approved Charon audition pauses 0.82 s; Modules 1 and 2 measure up to 1.04 s). Every clip was generated with the 1.6 s inner-pause gate (voice/gen_chapter.py MAX_INNER), the MetFix Module 1 and 2 recipe the owner approved on 2026-10-01.

_sync: The picture follows the voice (amendment H.74): each anchor [t, at, offset] lands build t on a sentence (an index, 0 first) or a phrase of the paragraph, at its first word plus offset seconds. Reveals land on their words: the rings sweep through the opening sentence and the spokes follow clockwise, each name landing as the voice lists it, strength to accuracy; the untrained skills dim on "different means", the green arc reaches each trained spoke as it is named ("Strength" to "flexibility"), Trained (organic) lands on "training: a measurable", the blue arc reaches "Coordination" to "accuracy" as they are named and Practiced (neural) lands on "practice"; the arcs meet on "meet", power and speed turn amber on "Power and speed" and Both lands on "both"; the generalist grows from "plot", is named on "the generalist" and rises into its prism by "broadly excellent", the dashed floor ring draws from "Its weakest skill" and touches the three weakest skills on "sets a floor", and Weakest skill 7 lands on "the floor sits high"; the powerlifter's dashed outline draws from "the powerlifter" to "metabolic demand", the gaps hatch through "Where it falls short of the generalist, the gaps open up", the floor collapses on "Its floor collapses" and catches on "endurance"; the wheel folds into the first of the thirteen cells as the others grow on "Here are thirteen athletes", their floors draw through "sorted by how high their floor" and SORTED BY WEAKEST SKILL lands on "floor sits".

ten.text: CrossFit's first model says there are ten general physical skills. Here they are, one spoke each: strength, stamina, endurance, flexibility, power, speed, coordination, agility, balance, and accuracy. You are as fit as you are competent in each.

trained-practiced.text: The skills are won by different means. Strength, stamina, endurance, and flexibility respond to training: a measurable, organic change in the body. Coordination, agility, balance, and accuracy respond to practice: a change in the nervous system.

both.source: MODULE_COPY skills keyPoints 3; SKILLS power and speed definitions
both.text: Two skills sit where the arcs meet. Power and speed come from both training and practice. Power is applying maximum force in minimum time. Speed is minimizing the cycle time of a repeated movement.

generalist.source: ARCHETYPES Generalist CrossFitter blurb; MODULE_COPY skills keyPoints 4
generalist.text: Now plot an athlete. This is the generalist: broadly excellent, the most balanced shape on the wheel, with no peaks and no gaps. Its weakest skill sets a floor, this dashed ring, and the floor sits high.

specialist.source: ARCHETYPES Powerlifter blurb; MODULE_COPY skills keyPoints 4
specialist.text: Now a specialist, the powerlifter: maximal strength, with little metabolic demand. Where it falls short of the generalist, the gaps open up. Its floor collapses, down to its endurance. You are only as fit as you are competent across all ten.

thirteen.source: MODULE_COPY skills s2; ARCHETYPES (a balanced athlete and twelve specialists)
thirteen.text: Here are thirteen athletes: a balanced generalist against twelve specialists, sorted by how high their floor sits. The generalist comes out on top. A program develops fitness to the extent it improves all ten skills.
